items.title: Form Studies — Paper, Foam, Wire
items.description:
A three-part hands-on study of three-dimensional form across very different materials.

**Paper:** concentric arcs cut and folded out of a flat sheet, then stood up — a small cathedral made by removing the right amount of nothing.

**Foam (thermocol):** a circle and three square modules carved into different depths of recess, exploring how mass changes when you take volume away from inside it.

**Wire:** a vocabulary of single-line objects — a snail, tulip, butterfly, jellyfish, wine glass, camera, drum, umbrella, the word *love* — each made by bending one continuous strand. A study in describing a thing using only its outline.

items.title: Weaving a Sustainable Future
items.description:
A textile-art installation exploring Kantha — the traditional embroidery of West Bengal and Bangladesh — through the story of Amma, a village elder whose stitches hold a community together. Using a 5W analysis (Where, When, Who, What, Why), the project ties this 19th-century craft to the UN Sustainable Development Goals, showing how slow, hand-stitched making becomes a quiet form of climate action and cultural memory.

Group project: Lakshay, Manvi, Pranshi, Amoli, Priyan.

items.title: Visual Design Foundations
items.description: Three foundation studies on how design speaks. **Product Analysis** breaks down a rabbit-themed helmet from multiple angles, listing its functional features (kipper-on-head, button-to-open windshield, air filter, silicone ear cushion). **Design Matrix** maps real-world brand logos onto the building blocks of design — dot, line, shape, form, colour, texture, pattern. **Colour Psychology** pairs eight colour families (black, pink, orange, red, green, blue, yellow, brown) with the moods they carry and the brands that lean into each.
